messages.subject: Re: circle
messages.body_plain:
(The following pertains to Splus for Win. I would assume the following 
function would work other systems, but I have not tested it.)

There are two kinds of circles one can make. For example in Splus for Win. 
ver 3.3, the font 'Symbols' will make circle whose size is independent of 
the x and y limits. [points(.2,.1,pch=1, cex=2, font=3)]

Using par's 'pin' and 'usr', the following function will plot a circle 
whose radius is correct on the y axis (default) or the x axis (yaxis = F).

-jrw

"circle" <- 
function(cx, cy, r, yaxis = T, ...)
{
#   cx, cy, coordinates for centre; r is radius
#   yaxis = T, radius is correct on the y axis
#   yaxis = F, radius is correct on the x axis    
#   DATE WRITTEN:  1994      LAST REVISED:   17 July 1995
#   AUTHOR:  John R. Wallace (jw at u.washington.edu)
#
        z <- (0:360 * pi)/180
        pin <- par()$pin
        usr <- par()$usr
        adj <- (pin[2]/pin[1])/((usr[4] - usr[3])/(usr[2] - usr[1]))
        if(yaxis) {
                x <- sin(z) * r * adj + cx
                y <- cos(z) * r + cy
        }
        else {
                x <- sin(z) * r + cx
                y <- cos(z) * r * 1/adj + cy
        }
        lines(x, y, ...)
        invisible()
}

mhall at rekihaku.ac.jp wrote:

> Is there a function or script for adding a circle or ellipse on a plot.
> What I want to do is draw an ellipse around a set of points on a plot when
> I know my center point and have my two radii.
> 

probably there is a beautiful package which does this sort of things,
and I would like to know about it.
In the meantime, the next function is a very crude option:

draw.ellipse <- function(center,r1,r2,npts=100,...){
  x<-seq(0,2*pi,length=npts)
  lines(center[1]+r1*cos(x),center[2]+r2*sin(x),...)
  invisible()
}
this produces an ellipse with axes parallel to the coordinate axes (only);
expample of use:
plot(runif(10),runif(10))
draw.ellipse(c(0.5,0.6),0.3,0.4)
draw.ellipse(c(0.2,0.6),0.2,0.14,col=2,lty=3)

regards
Adelchi Azzalini

5/19/99

Here is another simple version, but more general:

ellipse <-
function(b, C, df, level = 0.95, xlab = "", ylab = "",add=T)
# Plot an ellipse with "covariance matrix C, center b, and P-content
# level according the F(df[1],df[2]) distribution.
{
        d <- sqrt(diag(C))
        df <- c(2, df)
        phase <- acos(C[1, 2]/(d[1] * d[2]))
        angles <- seq( - (PI), PI, len = 51)
        mult <- sqrt(df[1] * qf(level, df[1], df[2]))
        xpts <- b[1] + d[1] * mult * cos(angles)
        ypts <- b[2] + d[2] * mult * cos(angles + phase)
        if(add) lines(xpts, ypts)
        else plot(xpts, ypts, type = "l", xlab = xlab, ylab = ylab)
}
